name: Moyamoya Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Research Committee on Moyamoya Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Bilateral stenosis or occlusion of the terminal portion of the internal carotid arteries and proximal portions of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries
Presence of abnormal vascular networks (moyamoya vessels) near the stenotic areas on angiography
Exclusion of other causes of similar vascular changes such as atherosclerosis, autoimmune disease, or Down syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral stenosis or occlusion of the distal internal carotid arteries with presence of moyamoya vessels on angiography and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Unilateral involvement may be considered probable Moyamoya disease but requires follow-up for confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Often presenting as hemiparesis or sensory disturbance
Common initial presentation especially in children

pathognomonic.symptomName: Moyamoya vessels visible on cerebral angiography
searchTerms: narrowed brain arteries with collateral vessels

common.notes: Focal or generalized seizures may occur
More common in adults than children

occasional.notes: Transient or persistent visual field defects
Speech difficulties due to ischemic events
Rare movement disorders secondary to basal ganglia ischemia

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic illness and cerebral ischemia
Rare complication due to impaired CSF circulation

laboratory: Exclusion of autoimmune markers and coagulation disorders
imaging: Cerebral angiography showing stenosis/occlusion of distal internal carotid arteries
MRI/MRA demonstrating ischemic lesions and vessel abnormalities
genetic: RNF213 gene mutations associated especially in East Asian populations
other: Neuropsychological testing may reveal cognitive deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of vascular risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia)
Absence of moyamoya collateral vessels on angiography
Inflammatory changes on vessel wall imaging
Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography

references: Research Committee on Moyamoya Disease, 2012 Diagnostic Criteria
Scott RM, Smith ER. Moyamoya Disease and Moyamoya Syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2009;360(12):1226-1237.
Kuroda S, Houkin K. Moyamoya disease: current concepts and future perspectives. Lancet Neurol. 2008;7(11):1056-1066.
